title: Study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of supportive mitomycin C administered via electric current in the treatment of non-muscle invasive bladder cancer versus the standard immunotherapy.
official: Multicenter clinical trial with medical device associated with a drug in an authorised therapeutic use for the treatment of CVNMI evaluating the efficacy and tolerability of the adyuvant treatment with EMDA-MMC versus standard BCG in patients with high grade CVNMI
summary: Main objective: To evaluate the efficacy of the adjuvant with EMDA-MMC (induction x6 weekly instillations and 1 year of maintenance) compared with the BCG standard (induction x6 weekly instillations and 1 year of maintenance) in the adjuvant treatment of High Grade NMLCC.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patients older than 18 years and life expectancy ≥ 5 years.
2. Patients able to give informed consent for the study.
3. Patients with primary non-muscle infiltrating urothelial non-muscle metamorphosed (NMIBC), uni- or multi-focal, stages Ta and T1, High Grade (2004 WHO), including old G2 High Grade and all G3.
4. Patients treated with optically complete TUR of the tumor and, when indicated by clinical guidelines, RE-RTU that must be performed within the first 6 weeks.
5. Negative bladder random biopsies for Tcis
6. Presence of own muscle in the TUR and / or in the RE-RTU.
7. RE-RTU in all cases of T1 and also in Ta tumors when the initial TUR is incomplete or with absence of muscle in the sample.
Exclusion criteria:
1. Patients unable to give informed consent for their participation in the study.
2. Stage tumors ≥T2.
3. cN + and / or cM + tumors.
4. Pregnant women.
5. Relative contraindications for the use of the EMDA system - Urethral stricture. - Giant prostatic lobe with bladder neck occlusion. - Psychosis - Alcoholism - Active untreated urinary infection
6. Patients with a history of allergic reactions to BCG or MMC.
7. Patients with pacemakers or DICs
8. Previous history of bladder tumors.
9. Antecedents of pelvic radiotherapy (bladder, prostate, rectum, vagina, uterus).
10. Absence of own muscle in the sample (neither in RTU nor in RE-RTU).
11. Patients with stage T1 who have not received RE-RTU.
12. Patients with Tcis isolated or associated with papillary tumor.
13. Presence of squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder or bladder adenocarcinoma
